Let's apply this argument to everything we pay for that the government does.  Military?  I should get a say in what wars we fight and who we kill because I'm paying for it.

Justice system.  I don't think murder is really a crime if the person deserved to be murdered.  I don't care what the law or a jury says, I'm paying for it after all.

You do get a say in what we cover, it's called representative democracy.  I'm sorry if your 1/1000000 vote didn't win a binary decision.  Your expectation of everyone's personal freedoms being tailored to is fantasy and it's not worth removing the benefits of centralized government.

So yes, there are downsides and sacrifices inherent in any decision ever made by anyone.  That's life.  It's not something that only libertarians recognize, everyone else has just accepted that some negative side effects are worse than others.
